events.description: The Christmas City Express is a storybook experience recommended for families with children and the young at heart. The performance begins in the Lake Superior Railroad Museum, where you’ll be treated to a classic book reading of the new Christmas City Express story, enjoy carolers, and a visit from a special guest! Then it’s time to hop on the train for a cheerful 30-minute ride out to Lake Superior’s shore — complete with holiday music, singalongs, some narration, twinkling lights, and all the warm fuzzy feelings. Onboard, you’ll be treated to complimentary hot chocolate and cookies to keep the magic going. This event is created with shorter attention spans in mind, making it a great fit for kids under 10 (though every year, we see grown-ups grinning just as much as the little ones). It’s sweet, simple, and pure holiday joy. About 90-minutes in total from arrival to finish.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings (nee Turany) and has a son, August, born in January 2003. Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally. His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock. 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life.

events.title: Iron County Historical Museum
events.description: Plan an adventure at the Iron County Historical Society Museum. Built in 1893 as the town hall for the now-vanished Town of Vaughn, the museum building was sold the following April to serve as the courthouse of Iron County. The Museum offers you three full floors of display from history of iron mining to railroads, timber to veterans, home life to faith based articles. The museum is filled with many old photos showing life in the past. May thru October MON/WED/FRI/SAT 1OAM-2PM, NOVEMBER - APRIL WED/FRI/SAT.

events.title: Shane Nelson - Havannas (Superior WI)
events.description: Live music with songwriter Shane Nelson -grab some authentic Cubin food, a drink and a seat, and enjoy an evening of listening. Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.venue: Superior and Douglas County Retail Stores/Restaurants/Liquor Store/Beauty Salons/Services
events.description: Are you ready for Small Business Saturday and Shop Small Superior Week? After scoring some Black Friday shopping deals, remember to save a bit of your holiday shopping for your local stores!The Superior-Douglas County Area Chamber of Commerce and theSuperior Business Improvement Districtare again teaming up to promoteSmall Business Saturdayin an effort to continually support and promote our local small businesses! In the coming weeks, the two organizations will work together to market this national shopping holiday (held every year on the Saturday after Thanksgiving and Black Friday) on a local level.This year we are excited to continue Shop Small Superior Week - beginning on Small Business Saturday, November 28 and running through December 5, 2026. This format allows customers the opportunity to shop over the course of a week vs. concentrating on just one day. It also allows businesses to participate that may have operating hours outside of the Small Business Saturday one-day event.Multiple Superior Businesses will be participating in this national shopping holiday by offering deals, discounts, samples, customer appreciation activities, and more!

events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund.

events.title: The Book of Bublé – Christmas
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: “The Book of Bublé – Christmas” is a high-octane holiday tribute to style, swagger, and swing. Emmy® winner Shaun Johnson and his seven-piece band deliver Michael Bublé’s biggest hits with powerhouse vocals and bold new orchestrations—from “Haven’t Met You Yet” to “Feeling Good,” and “Frosty the Snowman” to “It’s Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas.” Drawing on more than two decades of national touring, Shaun, longtime frontman of Tonic Sol-fa and an artist with a recent Top 5 Billboard brings both a vocalist’s and bandleader’s perspective to the repertoire, balancing high-energy performances with the familiar songs that define the season. Musicianship and ensemble work remain at the core, keeping the show fresh and fully in the moment. Backed by a seasoned seven-piece ensemble, The Book of Bublé channels the playful, confident style that earned Shaun multiple Entertainer of the Year nominations – a holiday concert that swings.

events.title: Traditional Swedish Lutefisk and Meatball Dinner
events.description: Traditional Swedish Lutefisk and Meatball dinner! Traditional Swedish Lutefisk and Meatball Dinners. Guests will enjoy a hearty all-you-care-to-eat meal of Swedish appetizers, lutefisk, Swedish meatballs, side dishes, and Swedish desserts prepared by Marnie, as learned from her parents and grandparents over the years. Come hear about the julbokka (the Christmas goat), the tomten (the good ones and the troublemakers), the lucky almond in the rice pudding, and other special Christmas traditions brought over by Marnie's family from Sweden more than 100 years ago! events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational. This recurring monthly event has no cover charge, though donations are always appreciated. Thank you Chickadee-Dee-Dee for leading us in song!

events.description: Plan an adventure at the Iron County Historical Society Museum. Built in 1893 as the town hall for the now-vanished Town of Vaughn, the museum building was sold the following April to serve as the courthouse of Iron County. The Museum offers you three full floors of display from history of iron mining to railroads, timber to veterans, home life to faith based articles. The museum is filled with many old photos showing life in the past. May thru October MON/WED/FRI/SAT 1OAM-2PM, NOVEMBER - APRIL WED/FRI/SAT.

Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. events.title: Still Learning 24: Estate Planning – A Practical Roadmap
events.description: This course will take place on the Thursday afternoons of Dec. 3 and 10, 2026, 2:00-5:00 p.m., with Attorney Roxanne Lutgen at the Mercer Community Center, or live via Zoom upon request. This two-day estate planning course provides a clear, practical roadmap for protecting your assets and family under Wisconsin law. Participants will explore essential lifetime legal tools, including 1) financial and healthcare powers of attorney, 2) comparing the mechanics of wills and trusts, 3) navigating the realities of the Wisconsin probate system, and finally 4) other strategies such as transfer-on-death deeds and beneficiary designations to avoid probate and ensure your estate passes smoothly to your loved ones. Requirements: Participants should have an interest in learning about estate planning. Roxanne Lutgen is a CPA and attorney who focuses in estate planning, probate, real estate and elder law at Lutgen Law Office LLC in Mercer, Wis. She has prior career experience in contract law, auditing, budgets, financial accounting, and higher education administration.. We recommend signing up at least two weeks ahead of class to ensure class fills and to prevent cancellation.

events.title: Veterans Memorial Hall Annual Remembrance Dinner on 12/03/2026
events.description: Purchase Tickets Online Join us for the 21st annual Veterans Memorial Hall Remembrance Dinner on Thursday, December 3, 2026, in the Great Hall at the St. Louis County Depot. This year’s keynote presentation, “Shipbuilding in the Twin Ports During World War II,” will be presented by Stephen B. Daniel. During World War II, shipyards throughout Duluth and Superior built military and support vessels for the war effort. Stephen Daniel will explore where these ships were built, the types of vessels produced, and the people who worked in the local shipyards, including the important role women played as many men left the region for military service. The evening begins with a social hour at 5:00 p.m., followed by dinner at 6:00 p.m. and the keynote presentation at 7:00 p.m. Dinner will be catered by Valentini’s, and guests may also participate in a silent auction. Tickets are $65 per person. Join us for an evening of remembrance and local history, highlighting the remarkable contribution the Twin Ports made to America’s World War II effort.

events.title: Dead North + Death Valley Yacht Club
events.venue: Cedar Lounge Earth Rider Brewery taproom
events.description: Dead North is a progressive bluegrass band from the northwoods of Michigan’s Keweenaw Peninsula. Now residing in Minneapolis, the band is composed of Luke Pascot (guitar, vocals, banjo) and Kora Melia (mandolin, fiddle, vocals). Together, they push the limits of the bluegrass genre with bold experimentation while still maintaining a high level of respect for tradition. Their sound elegantly mixes bluegrass with elements of jazz, rock, country, funk, and so much more. Influenced by the likes of Tony Rice, Billy Strings, David Grisman, etc., Dead North is a must see for any fans of progressive acoustic music. Death Valley Yacht Club's signature sound features their intricate vocal harmonies sung over the interplay between their tightly-arranged acoustic guitars. MN Songbird described the band's sound as “timeless”, saying they could imagine hearing the music “in the 90’s opening for someone like Elliott Smith.” Their original music takes inspiration from artists like The Beatles, Neil Young, The Avett Brothers, and Jesse Welles.

Tickets are $8 for adults and $5 for students. Thank you to our movie sponsor: Wakefield Winter Wonderlights! Synopsis: On Christmas Eve, a skeptical young boy begins to doubt the existence of Santa Claus. Just before midnight, a mysterious steam train known as the Polar Express abruptly pulls up outside his home. Invited aboard by the enigmatic Conductor, he joins a group of other children on an extraordinary journey to the North Pole. Along the track, the children encounter daunting obstacles, strange wilderness figures, and moments that test their courage and friendship. Upon reaching the heart of Santa’s sprawling city, the young protagonist learns that the true magic of Christmas lies not in what you see, but in what you choose to believe—symbolized by a silver sleigh bell whose ring can only be heard by those who truly believe.

events.description: Cuban food and songwriting, From Shane Nelson Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.description: Sunhee’s Little Table at Bent Paddle 🍜 Sunhee’s Little Table is bringing authentic Korean flavors to Bent Paddle for a pop-up you won’t want to miss. Here’s a taste of what they’ll be serving up: Bulgogi (불고기) Thinly sliced beef marinated in a savory mix of soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and a touch of sweetness—then grilled to perfection. Rich, flavorful, and made for pairing with a cold beer. Tteokbokki (떡볶이) A Korean street food favorite featuring chewy rice cakes in a spicy-sweet chili sauce. Bold, comforting, and just the right amount of heat. Bulgogi Kimbap (불고기 김밥) Korean-style rolls packed with marinated bulgogi, fresh veggies, and rice, all wrapped in seaweed. Easy to snack on and perfect alongside your favorite Bent Paddle pour. Come hungry, grab a drink, and enjoy something a little different in the Taproom.

events.description: Join the Volunteers of Spooner Health as they hold their 36th annual Love Light Tree Ceremony on Monday, December 7 at 2:00 p.m. The event will be held at Spooner Health and streamed live on Facebook (@SpoonerHealth). For those attending in person, there will be refreshments after the event. This event is organized by Betsy Andrea of the Volunteers of Spooner Health and will feature an inspirational message from Mary Hemshrot, as well as music by Tim Kern. Mike Schafer, Spooner Health CEO, will welcome everyone and read the names of all those for whom lights were purchased. All proceeds go towards various Volunteers of Spooner Health projects. Community members can make a minimum donation of $5 and “purchase” a red, blue or white light. A red light is in honor of someone, a blue light is for peace or for someone who has or is currently serving our country and a white light is in memory of someone. Previous years have seen over 120 lights placed on the tree to honor and remember loved ones.

events.title: Pearl Harbor Documentary Showing
events.description: Could world history have unfolded differently if Washington had listened to a man from Spooner, Wisconsin? That’s the question explored in a new locally produced history documentary, showing Pearl Harbor Day, December 7 at 11:00 a.m. and 6:30 p.m. at The Palace Theater in Spooner, Wis. George Washington Harmon, a former mayor and longtime Spooner resident, detailed highly specific information regarding an imminent attack in a letter addressed to the White House dated ten days before the attack on Pearl Harbor. The letter warns of Japanese aircraft carriers, approximate positions, Hawaii as the intended target, and even references to midget submarines. Learn more at one of the showings on Pearl Harbor Day. Pearl Harbor Prophet will be presented twice on Pearl Harbor Day, December 7, 2026, at The Palace Theater, 238 Walnut St., Spooner, WI 54801. The 11:00 a.m. screening will include a livestream of the Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day ceremony hosted by VFW Post 137 Proctor-Duluth at the Lake Superior Maritime Visitor Center in Duluth, Minnesota. Bartosh will also share the story of George W. Harmon's warning during the event. The 6:30 p.m.

events.description: The Holiday Cookie Exchange is back! Previously held at the Mercer Public Library, this year’s exchange will take place at the Northwoods Hub (Mercer Senior Center) on Monday, December 7th at 11:30 a.m. The library will not be hosting a separate exchange this year. Here’s how it works: Bring 3 dozen of your favorite homemade cookies and head home with 3 dozen assorted cookies from the other bakers. Be sure to bring a container to take your cookies home in, and if you’re willing to share your recipe, bring a copy of that too. You can sign up in advance at the Hub or just come on December 7th. events.title: Art on Tap With Eric Klepinger Creating Live Edge Wooden Ornaments
events.description: Join us for another fun and creative evening of Art on Tap at Castle Danger Brewery! Each class is led by professional artist and Voyageur Artists member Eric Klepinger. For this class, each participant will be given some hand-made live edge mini-wooden disks, which will be all ready prepared for painting on. We will provide enough for each participant to create at least 12 ornaments, maybe more. It is super fun to create micro painting on small wooden disks as each one is very unique. Ribbon will also be provided so you can add a way to hang your ornaments. Class is $15 for Voyageur Members, $20 for non-members and $10 for Castle Danger Staff. Class is limited to 16 people, no experience necessary and all the materials will be supplied. Please click on the ‘Tickets’ link to sign-up and arrive by 5:15 pm to secure your place. The ‘Tickets’ link becomes inactive by 3:15 pm on the day of the class. Walk-ins are welcome based on available space.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.description: Join other makers and crafters weekly at the Ely Folk School for a relaxed morning of creativity and sharing. Whether you crochet, quilt, solder, write, or weave, any project is welcome. This space is also excellent for students who did not finish a project during their class. All are welcome, no matter skill level or (reasonable) project type. A space to share projects and work in a community setting are important! Drop in whenever as you like, for as long as you like. events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free!

events.title: Volunteer Hand Pie Assembly
events.description: Join us during our usual Makers Morning for a special volunteer event aimed at getting us prepped for our Winter Bonfire! Volunteers will take pre-made pie dough (created by staff and students the night before at the “Do It Yourself Hand Pies” class) and assembly them into delectable savory hand pies. Ingredients may include zucchini, onion, mushrooms, garlic, and fresh herbs! We need all hands on deck to make enough hand pies for the Winter Bonfire on December 12th, where we celebrate the return of the land to ice and snow, and prepare for a season of communal rest and reset. This fun annual event is a great way to contribute to the community event, and glean some tips and tricks for assembling your own hand pies in the future. All ingredients and equipment will be provided by the Ely Folk School (including aprons) so just show up to help out.

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational.

events.title: The Last High-rah OR The Day That Never Was | the fate of hemp awaits
events.description: The fate of hemp awaits. We're throwing a party. Because that's what we do. High or Low this community is amazing and deserves to be recognized. Whether we're celebrating hemp beverages finding a path forward or mourning a chapter of the industry as we pick up the pieces and keep fighting into 2027 and beyond, one thing is certain: we're not going quietly. This is about more than a beverage. It's an industry, a community, a way of life, and for many, a pathway to better well-being, connection and social moments. The fate of hemp may be decided by the time we gather, but either way, we're showing up. Let's gather, celebrate, connect, educate and organize. Party: 6–9 PM Live music from Rory Van James Band: 6–8 PM Special guests, glass sales, education and conversations around growing your own, with more community partners popping in along the way. No cover. No problem. Support us through a purchase, raise a can because we can. Whatever the outcome, hemp has a future worth fighting for. Come raise a cana beverage or beer with us.

events.title: Wisconsin Life Listening Party - Makers' Edition
J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | The Ore House
events.description: J Streitz plays original folk/Americana songs along with a few covers by great songwriters including John Prine, Todd Snider, and Bob Dylan. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.description: Join us on a frozen night in December as we wake the city up from it's hibernation. Hometown hero's Pronoya come back in town and they brought some friends. In late 2019 (just before the Great Plague swept the world), a great hunger was stirring within the bowels of St. Peter, MN. In order to satiate this carnivorous desire, members of HeirAfire, Faulter, and Alation congregated within a dank basement. From within this basement, a pact was made to deliver the most melodious metal that Southern Minnesota has ever seen.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz & Jimmy Rogers | Sir Bens Tavern
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: J Streitz and Jimmy Rogers play original Midwest folk/Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: GB Leighton
events.description: The Event Center, Floodwood GB Leighton acoustic show The Event Center, Floodwood 201 West 7th Avenue Floodwood, MN 55736 More than 200 shows a year. Jubilant fans who follow him from Minnesota to Mexico. More than 100,000 albums sold. A new release “Get Up” and a state-of-the-art nightclub named after one of his songs -- all without the support of a major record label... Meet GB Leighton, a band named after one of the regions’ most incendiary live performers and consistently solid songwriters, Brian Leighton. Through more than a decade and eleven studio albums, Leighton and his five piece band have been tearing up rock clubs, festivals and even a few fan’s living rooms with a slew of songs that connect with the heart and couples singing along out on the dance floor. “A man of the people” is a phrase usually reserved for statesmen and politicians, but for Leighton, it’s a fitting description when you see him in action working a crowd. Leighton delivers that same inescapable rock ‘n’ roll spirit night after night. “If I hadn’t heard a bunch of Bruce’s bootlegs or seen the videos I’d be a much different musician,” he says today.

events.description: The Geminids meteor shower occurs between November 19 to December 24 and this year will peak on the nights of December 13 and 14. The meteor shower's radiant is located in the constellation Gemini, which rises around sunset.

The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | Ursa Minor Brewing
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music along with a few covers. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album.

King is an accomplished pianist, songwriter and producer with a career spanning live performance, recording and touring. Covert comes from the world of stand-up comedy and has performed alongside nationally known comedians including Jeff Ross. Put the two together, and things got hilariously inappropriate pretty quickly. King and Covert only met in February 2026, but what began as an experiment combining live music and stand-up comedy quickly gained an audience. Drooling Pianos has already sold out multiple performances, including its debut, and received an enthusiastic response during its Twin Ports appearance at Clyde Iron Works this summer.

events.description: The Snowman is back at the Reif with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra for a second December, on its way to becoming a Grand Rapids tradition. events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz & Jimmy Rogers | Sir Bens Tavern
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.title: Indecent Proposal
events.description: Indecent Proposal is coming back to Mr. D’s Bar & Grill in Duluth, MN on Saturday, December 19th for their Ugly Sweater Xmas Party from 8 PM–midnight. Throw on the worst sweater you own, grab a drink, and come party with us before the holidays fully take over. We’ll bring the covers, originals, big guitars, and the kind of night that makes an ugly sweater feel like a power move. Come get weird, festive, and Indecent at Mr. D’s. Come out and get Indecent 😈😎🎸🤘💜 www.indyp218.com Indecent Proposal is a band out of Duluth, Minnesota, built around connection, feel, and songs that hold up in a room full of people. Blending modern alt-rock, groove-driven covers, and emotionally grounded originals, the band focuses on moments you can feel as much as hear. Their live shows move fluidly between intimacy and release—quiet verses, loud hearts, and choruses that come back at you from the crowd. Led by frontman Josh Brown, with Selie’s dynamic vocals, Jason Soderlund on guitar, Terry Beckman on bass, and Andy Fabian on drums, Indecent Proposal brings intention to every set and honesty to every song.

events.title: Ian Alexy: Every Third Saturday at Sir Ben's
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Ian Alexy plays solo acoustic (with looping and effects, of course) on the third Saturday of every month at Sir Benedict's in Duluth. Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life.

events.title: Sunhee's Little Table - Authentic Korean Food Truck
events.description: Sunhee’s Little Table at Bent Paddle 🍜 Sunhee’s Little Table is bringing authentic Korean flavors to Bent Paddle for a pop-up you won’t want to miss. Come grab a pint (or THC bev) and dig into some seriously good, made-from-scratch Korean comfort food. Here’s a taste of what they’ll be serving up: Bulgogi (불고기) Thinly sliced beef marinated in a savory mix of soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and a touch of sweetness—then grilled to perfection. Rich, flavorful, and made for pairing with a cold beer. Tteokbokki (떡볶이) A Korean street food favorite featuring chewy rice cakes in a spicy-sweet chili sauce. Bold, comforting, and just the right amount of heat. Bulgogi Kimbap (불고기 김밥) Korean-style rolls packed with marinated bulgogi, fresh veggies, and rice, all wrapped in seaweed. Easy to snack on and perfect alongside your favorite Bent Paddle pour. Come hungry, grab a drink, and enjoy something a little different in the Taproom.

events.title: December Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 2nd of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. December's full moon is known as the Cold Moon or Long Nights Moon. In addition to the shortest daylight day of the year, the Long Nights Moon pertains to the amount of time the moon is above the horizon. It takes a high trajectory across the sky because it is opposite to the low sun.

events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Jazz at the Lake Superior Railroad Museum
events.description: JAZZ at the Depot Returns! Great jazz. Historic trains. Good food and drinks. What better way to spend a winter Saturday? One of Duluth’s favorite winter traditions is back! JAZZ at the Depot, sponsored by Krenzen, brings the sounds of live jazz to the historic Lake Superior Railroad Museum inside the St. Louis County Depot in downtown Duluth. Every Saturday afternoon throughout the winter season, continuing through April, enjoy live music from the former Club Saratoga Jazz Quartet, performing trackside among the museum’s historic locomotives and railcars. From the swinging big-band sounds of Duke Ellington, Count Basie and Glenn Miller to the timeless tunes of Benny Goodman, Thelonious Monk and other jazz greats, there’s something for longtime jazz fans and casual listeners alike. Led by Randy Lee, the quartet delivers an afternoon of classic favorites, modern jazz and entertaining musical commentary. Make an afternoon of it! Admission is just $7 per person, including the cash bar. Warm up with complimentary coffee and hot cocoa, or grab something tasty from the concession stand, featuring gourmet hot dogs, snacks and freshly popped popcorn.

events.description: 3rd of 3 supermoons A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. The January full moon is most often known as the Wolf Moon because it is the month hungry wolves howl in the night. It is also known as the Stay Home, or Quiet, Moon as cold temps set in and we want to snuggle in and stay home.

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational. This recurring monthly event has no cover charge, though donations are always appreciated. Thank you Chickadee-Dee-Dee for leading us in song!

events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

Summer race course improvements include adding curves to a few sharp corners and widening the Highlands Aid Station area. Larger indoor warming area near Start Line. There is now a 15K "Low Snow Loop" located completely at ABR that can be used in case there is not enough snow to facilitate finishing in downtown Ironwood. "Finnish" Line in Ironwood's Downtown City Square. 5K Hauska Hiihto Fun Ski, and Depot Dash for kids on Friday. While the COVID-19 pandemic seems behind us, we do still ask anyone with symptoms of illness to remain home. It involves a combination of stamina, perseverance, courage, and determination held in reserve for hard times.

events.title: Claire & Ellen's Winter Book Club
events.description: Join us for a deeper dive into books with some great company with Claire Duquette & Ellen Akins. Second Wednesdays Nov-April 6-7pm. Nov 11 Yesteryear, Caro Claire Burke Dec 9 Mrs. Caliban, Rachel Ingalls Jan 13 The Tiger’s Wife, Tea Obreht Feb 10 Small things Like These, Claire Keegan March 10 Life After Life, Kate Atkinson April 14 Sea of Tranquility, Emily St. John Mandel Everyone Welcome. You do not need to “join.” Come whenever it works or the book strikes your fancy. The Book Bar will be open serving wine, cider, beer & NA drinks + sandwiches and pizzas. Claire Duquette is the former editor of the Ashland Daily Press and continues to write about books and the arts. She is the assistant manager at Honest Dog Books where you’ll find her behind the counter Saturdays selecting books for the store’s SurpriseMe! Subscription. Ellen Akins is the author of the novels Home Movie (1988), Little Woman (1990), Public Life (1993), and Hometown Brew (1998), and the short story collection World Like a Knife (1991). She writes book reviews for national publications like the Washington Post and Star Tribune and loves talking books. Recurring monthly on the 2nd Wednesday.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: The Last Revel
events.description: The Last Revel is a four-piece folk group from Minneapolis, Minnesota. Utilizing their multi-instrumental abilities, members Lee Henke, Ryan Acker, and Vincenzio Donatelle, bring a full spectrum of modern Americana to life with lush arrangements of three-part vocal harmonies, acoustic guitar, upright bass, fiddle, and 5-string banjo to consistently support impassioned performances of their honest and heartfelt songwriting. Drawing influence from their salt of the earth Midwest ethos the band’s songs so naturally blend the genres of Folk, Old Time String-Band and Indie Rock to create a sound that echoes the current heartbeat of America. The Last Revel released their brand new album, Gone For Good, produced by Dave Simonett of Trampled by Turtles on Thirty Tigers on July 18th, 2025.

He is known around the world for his unique brand of humor, which largely revolves around his observations on life. Gaffigan is a top ten comedian according to Forbes’ most recent comedy list and top ten earning comedian in Pollstar. events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | Ursa Minor Brewing
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music along with a few covers. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album.

events.title: The Ok Factor
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Olivia Diercks and Karla Peters – cellist and violinist of the new-classical crossover duo, The OK Factor – have one word to describe their musical connection: lucky. The almost telepathic way they respond to one another is palpable to the audiences they capture during performances, as is their spontaneity and joy. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh, and have been described as “genre-bending” (Julie Amacher, MPR) and “pure magic” (Wausau Pilot & Review). In their 10+ years of writing, performing, and touring, The OK Factor has honed the ways they impact communities outside the concert hall. Residency work has become a deep passion – sharing intimate performances, conducting outreach activities, and leading workshops for students through their education initiative, ATLAS. Olivia and Karla are also sought-after collaborators and composers-in-residence, having worked with many regional, national, and international artists, and various digital music libraries.

events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.title: Flo Rida: Whistle & Whiskey Tour
events.description: With special guests Mitchell Tenpenny and Jay Webb Wednesday, February 3, 2027 | AMSOIL Arena | 7:00pm HERE Get ready for one unforgettable night as global superstar Flo Rida and multi-platinum country hitmaker Mitchell Tenpenny team up for the Whistle & Whiskey Tour, with Jay Webb kicking off the party! Whistle & Whiskey brings together the massive hits and nonstop energy of a Flo Rida show with the sound of Mitchell’s country music for a night built to keep fans on their feet. From country favorites to some of the biggest party anthems of the past two decades, the tour brings three artists and three distinct sounds together on one stage. Headlining the night is Flo Rida, one of the most recognizable hitmakers and live performers of his generation. Since exploding onto the scene with the 7x Platinum “Low” featuring T-Pain, which spent 10consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, Flo Rida has delivered hit after hit, including “Right Round,” “Club Can’t Handle Me,” “Good Feeling,” “Wild Ones,” “Whistle” and “My House.” With well over100 million singles sold worldwide, his catalog has become the soundtrack to parties around the world.

events.title: Jay Webb
events.description: Country artist Jay Webb writes songs that hit like a gut punch. Raised between the backroads of North Alabama and the city in the south, music was how he made sense of the chaos around him. What started as a way to process a turbulent childhood quickly became his purpose — gritty storytelling over genre-blurring beats, delivered with zero filter. He started cutting demos in high school and never stopped, releasing track after track on his own and building a following from the ground up. His lyrics cut deep, his voice carries the scars and his sound refuses to stay in one lane. Webb doesn’t clean up the mess — he leans into it, and has a good time doing it. Pulling from a wide range of influences, he pairs the weight of Johnny Cash and Hank Williams with the edge of Juice WRLD and Post Malone. It’s not traditional country — and he doesn’t want it to be. He calls it “music for real people with real problems,” and his fans know exactly what that means. In 2022, a viral TikTok pushed his music to a wider audience. Since then, he’s dropped standout tracks like “Down Here,” “Bury Me With Bourbon” and “Broken,” racking up over 415M streams and more than 2M fans.

events.title: Mitchell Tenpenny
events.description: Six years into his record deal with Columbia Records, Mitchell Tenpenny is leaning in even more. On his new album “The 3rd,” the Nashville native is leaning into his story, his fans, his roots and his influences – all with an eye on the future. Country radio knows Tenpenny as a reliable hitmaker and husky-voiced storyteller with an ear for undeniable hooks and unforgettable melodies. Fans who care to listen deeper recognize that he not only produces country radio smashes but is also a genre disruptor unafraid of punctuating his country storytelling with edgy lyrics, hard-driving drum beats and heavy guitars. “The 3rd” is Tenpenny’s most authentic – and adventurous – album yet. Named after a song that was named after him, “The 3rd” is a testament to his personal growth and artistic evolution. No longer playing games, Tenpenny has crafted an album that resonates with his own experiences and emotions. This honest and empathetic collection showcases his maturity as a man, singer, songwriter, and storyteller and invites listeners to join him on his creative journey through life and music. “I want this record to be all over the place,” Tenpenny said.

events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Sam Miltich with the Itasca Orchestra
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Grand Rapids’ own Sam Miltich joined the Hot Club of San Francisco as a teenager and has since toured internationally and played Lincoln Center. This February he brings his band home to share the Reif stage with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra: Sam on guitar, his father Matthew Miltich on bass, plus other instruments. The music travels. Choro (SHOH-roo) is the quick, bright instrumental music of Rio de Janeiro. The Nuevo Tango from Argentina. Čoček (CHO-chek) is the Romani dance music of the Balkans. And Sam got his start in the swinging guitar jazz Django Reinhardt made famous in 1930s Paris. For the finale, young string players from IOSP’s programs in Grand Rapids, Bigfork, and Remer join the band and the orchestra for one big celebration of music. It’s a February night out of the cold, with musicians of every age on one stage.

events.title: Daughtry
events.description: Daughtry, one of the most visible and best-selling rock bands of the 21st century, has sold out concerts across the globe. Their debut album, the self-titled Daughtry, was the top-selling album of 2007 and was the fastest selling rock debut album in Soundscan history. The record was nominated for 4 GRAMMY® Awards and won 4 American Music Awards, alongside 7 Billboard Music Awards, including “Album of the Year.” Subsequent albums, Leave This Town (2009), Break The Spell (2011), and Baptized (2013) have all gone Platinum, with Cage To Rattle (2018) certified Gold. In 2021, the band released their record Dearly Beloved, with singles “World On Fire,” “Heavy Is The Crown,” and “Changes Are Coming,” all cracking the Top 10. Following yet another Top 10 success with their 2023 smash cover of Journey’s “Separate Ways (Worlds Apart)" featuring Halestorm's Lzzy Hale, Daughtry ushered in a new sonic era with their debut Big Machine Records single, “Artificial.” The return to their rock roots scored the band their first No. 1 single at the Active Rock format, laying the groundwork for their new EP, set to release this fall.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | Ursa Minor Brewing
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music along with a few covers. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: Our Town
events.description: Theatre North Presents: Our Town, by Thornton Wilder, Directed by: Helen Fashbaugh Show Dates and Times: February 18, 19, 20, 26 and 27 at 7:00pm Matinees February 21 and 28 at 2:00pm Thornton Wilder’s American classic, Pultizer-prize winning Our Town, explores the universal human experience of life, love, and death. Set in the fictional small town of Grover’s Corners, New Hampshire, the story follows the everyday lives of the Gibbs and Webb families across three acts. The play is famous for its minimalist approach, often performed on a bare stage with no curtains or scenery, relying on pantomime and a narrator called the Stage Manager to guide the audience into its intimacy and truth. The narrative is divided into three distinct acts: Act I: Daily Life: Introduces the town’s routine, highlighting the simple chores, gossip, and rhythms of small-town life. Act II: Love and Marriage: Follows the childhood friends, George Gibbs and Emily Webb, as they fall in love, grow up, and get married. Act III: Death and Eternity: Concludes years later with Emily’s tragic death in childbirth.

events.title: Guys On Ice – An Ice Fishing Musical
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The show follows two lifelong pals, Marvin and Lloyd, as they spend a day in their ice shanty doing everything but catching fish. More than just a play, Guys on Ice is a musical tribute to the stubborn resilience of Midwesterners. Featuring show-stopping numbers like “De Wishing Hole,” “Fish is de Miracle Food,” and the legendary “Ode to a Snowmobile Suit” (featuring a zipper dance routine you have to see to believe), this production captures the heart, the humor, and the “oh-fer-cute” charm of life on the ice.

events.title: Guys On Ice
events.description: Grab your thermos, drill a hole in the ice, and settle in for the hilarious musical comedy about friendship, fishing, and frozen winters. The Quintessential Comedy of the North From the land of ten thousand lakes to the frozen bays of the Great Lakes, Guys on Ice is hitting the road to celebrate the secret language of the North: ice fishing. This beloved musical comedy invites audiences into a world where the beer is cold, the stove is warm, and the wisdom is as thick as the ice on the lake. More than just a play, Guys on Ice is a musical tribute to the stubborn resilience of Midwesterners. Featuring show-stopping numbers like "De Wishing Hole," "Fish is de Miracle Food," and the legendary "Ode to a Snowmobile Suit" (featuring a zipper dance routine you have to see to believe), this production captures the heart, the humor, and the "oh-fer-cute" charm of life on the ice.

events.title: NEEDTOBREATHE
events.description: Despite a 20-year history that includes all the accolades of an iconic band, GRAMMY-nominated, multi-platinum band NEEDTOBREATHE came into their latest studio album with a much different frame of mind. They still felt they had something to prove. In truth, this is a band who have loomed large for years, leveraging a unique fusion of modern rock, purpose-driven soul and irresistible pop appeal into a stat line which puts them in exceedingly rare company. They’ve placed five Number One albums all across the Billboard chart spectrum, from Rock and Alternative. They’ve racked up two billion career streams and scored multi-platinum chart topping hits – “Brother” (feat. Gavin DeGraw), “Who Am I,” “Let’s Stay Home Tonight” and dozens more. And they’ve done it all while filling venues across the globe. Ask their fans and it’s been two decades of spirit-mining songs, master musicianship and elemental artistry, digging deep to create a series of sonic monuments to the human condition. Their most recent effort follows suit.

events.title: NEEDTOBREATHE
events.description: NEEDTOBREATHE has established itself as one of the most dynamic and influential bands in modern rock. Known for their powerful live shows and emotionally resonant songwriting, the band has released a string of critically acclaimed albums, earned multiple GRAMMY nominations, and built a devoted audience around the world. Their music blends rock, Americana, soul, and gospel influences into a sound that is uniquely their own, anchored by songs that speak to perseverance, faith, redemption, and the shared human experience. On November 19, the band is set to release The Long Surrender and The Fellow Passengers of Pain, the deluxe edition of their acclaimed album The Long Surrender.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: Our Town
events.description: Theatre North Presents: Our Town, by Thornton Wilder, Directed by: Helen Fashbaugh Show Dates and Times: February 18, 19, 20, 26 and 27 at 7:00pm Matinees February 21 and 28 at 2:00pm Thornton Wilder’s American classic, Pultizer-prize winning Our Town, explores the universal human experience of life, love, and death. Set in the fictional small town of Grover’s Corners, New Hampshire, the story follows the everyday lives of the Gibbs and Webb families across three acts. The play is famous for its minimalist approach, often performed on a bare stage with no curtains or scenery, relying on pantomime and a narrator called the Stage Manager to guide the audience into its intimacy and truth. The narrative is divided into three distinct acts: Act I: Daily Life: Introduces the town’s routine, highlighting the simple chores, gossip, and rhythms of small-town life. Act II: Love and Marriage: Follows the childhood friends, George Gibbs and Emily Webb, as they fall in love, grow up, and get married. Act III: Death and Eternity: Concludes years later with Emily’s tragic death in childbirth.

This “garage band” from Topeka released their debut album in 1974 after being discovered by Wally Gold, who worked for Don Kirshner, and have gone on to sell more than 30 million albums worldwide. Composing a catalogue that includes sixteen studio albums and five live albums, KANSAS has produced eight gold albums, three sextuple-Platinum albums (Leftoverture, Point of Know Return, Best of KANSAS), one platinum live album (Two for the Show), one quadruple-Platinum single ‘Carry On Wayward Son,’ and another triple-Platinum single ‘Dust in the Wind.’ KANSAS appeared on the Billboard charts for over 200 weeks throughout the ‘70’s and ‘80’s and played to sold-out arenas and stadiums throughout North America, Europe and Japan.

events.title: A Play: Walter Cronkite is Dead
events.description: THE STORY : A fierce thunderstorm has shut down airports up and down the East Coast. Two women, who appear to have nothing in common, are stuck in a waiting area at Reagan National Airport. Patty is a chatty southerner—a blue-collar woman from a red state—who is almost physically unable to tolerate silence. Margaret is a Washingtonian, reserved, educated, liberal and not interested in sharing her thoughts, or her table, with Patty. Forced together for a long night in a public place, the two strangers have no choice but to share a bottle of wine and begin to talk...and to listen. Their conversation is funny, difficult, deeply revealing and astonishingly frank. Patty and Margaret share details of their lives that lead them to a place of kinship neither of them could have imagined. Yes, Walter Cronkite is dead, but his wisdom and compassion lives on in this insightful comedy about what might be possible if people from opposite sides of the political aisle would stop shouting and take even one night to listen.

events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: Ski North Ultra
events.description: Ski North Ultra is an ultra-distance 100K cross-country skiing classic-only event along the North Shore of Lake Superior. The event has 38K and 100K options, following the Norpine, Cascade River State Park and Bally Creek trail systems near Lutsen, MN. This is a unique cross-country ski event. It is classic-skiing only, and will be on a mix of double-track and single-track ski trails. The trails are incredibly beautiful, and also very technical. The trails can be narrow, have sharp turns, have two-way traffic, and the terrain along Lake Superior can mean long, 20-30 minute climbs, and higher speed descents. The 100K race uses advanced courses. The 38K stays on intermediate trails, but please consider if this is the right fit for your skill level. This is a tough course. March snow conditions can be varying, and can also be the most wonderful time of year to enjoy skiing. The event is more of an adventure than a race. Come with an open mind and adventurous spirit, and you will have a great day. Kind, helpful volunteers and a spread of food will be available at aid stations every 10-15km throughout the race. Start and finish in Cascade River State Park.

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | The Ore House
events.description: J Streitz plays original folk/Americana songs along with a few covers by great songwriters including John Prine, Todd Snider, and Bob Dylan. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.description: Join the Ely Folk School on Thanksgiving for a potluck at 11am! We would love for you to bring something to share, though it is not required. EFS will ensure there is turkey! Please bring whatever you feel energized about making (or purchasing).

events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational. This recurring monthly event has no cover charge, though donations are always appreciated. Thank you Chickadee-Dee-Dee for leading us in song!

events.description: Trolls JR. is based on the irreverent DreamWorks Animation movie franchise and features a colorful, wondrous world populated by hilariously unforgettable characters. The show follows the overly optimistic Trolls, constantly with a song on their lips, and the comically pessimistic Bergens, who are only happy when they have Trolls in their stomach. The Troll thespians in Poppy’s company live by their motto: the show must go on. But when a tyrannical foreign emissary arrives in Bergenland, expectations are raised, forcing the Trolls to totally rework their show or risk being served up in the name of diplomacy by a Chef rehired and out for revenge.
